title: Tested twice, just to be sure
body:
A couple of months on… One very important biopsy, tested twice just to be sure, later.

A tiny 1-2% of pancreatic cancers happen to be neuroendocrine (called a PNET, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour) rather than adenocarcinoma. And that’s what the biopsy came back with.

It changes the prognosis from a potential number of months to possibly a few years left. The best of a bad situation, but still great news!

A PNET is generally slower growing and can be more responsive to treatment. The treatment can have fewer side effects as well. It can affect multiple sites in the body. In Dad's case, it's affecting the pancreas's hormone production, which is giving him a third type of diabetes (Type 3a) which looks a lot like type 2 but isn't associated with diet or lifestyle factors. Validation of his persistence that there's nothing wrong with his diet! It's also in his liver and lymph nodes, with possibly a tiny spot in his pelvis, but at the moment this doesn't seem to be affecting him as much.

Dad's PNET is grade 2 of 3, which defines how quickly the tumour's growing, so it's not the slowest but not the fastest.

Before the biopsy there were some scarily well timed appointments and problems that cropped up. The first signs of any impact on the stomach just happened to be on the same day as the oncologist appointment, which were well spotted by Dylan and meant radiation therapy the next day. His blood sugars started to get out of control just in time to get a comprehensive plan in place before chemo started. It felt like Divine intervention.

It’s been difficult to feel as good as the news is to be honest. Loss aversion but with grief. It doesn’t mean that it’s hard to focus on the positives though. And there’s time for plenty more good news to come!

It definitely takes a bit of pressure off. Meant Dad could enjoy Lucy’s graduation, there’s more time for Dad and Jane to sort out the house and all the other parts of life, Josh, Lucy and Cam could get away to Europe without any regret and it gives me more options to spend time at home.

All in all, things are in a much better place than the last post.

— Nick
